title: If only: hubiera sabido, habría venido
summary: Talk about what could have been: si hubiera…, habría…, mixed conditionals, ojalá, como si and reproaches.
focus: Pluperfect subjunctive and perfect conditional in counterfactuals
content:
## The two compound forms

Both are **haber + participle**. The pluperfect subjunctive has two equivalent sets of endings, and **-ra** is more common in speech.

| person | pluperfect subjunctive | perfect conditional |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **hubiera / hubiese** hablado | **habría** hablado |
| tú | **hubieras / hubieses** hablado | **habrías** hablado |
| él / ella / usted | **hubiera / hubiese** hablado | **habría** hablado |
| nosotros | **hubiéramos / hubiésemos** hablado | **habríamos** hablado |
| vosotros | **hubierais / hubieseis** hablado | **habríais** hablado |
| ellos / ustedes | **hubieran / hubiesen** hablado | **habrían** hablado |

## Past counterfactuals

To imagine a different past: **si + pluperfect subjunctive**, then **perfect conditional**.

- *Si **hubiera sabido** que venías, **habría hecho** una tarta.* (If I had known you were coming, I'd have made a cake.)

In speech the main clause often uses **hubiera** too: *…te **hubiera** llamado*. Both are standard. The si-clause **never** takes habría: *si habría sabido* is wrong.

## Mixed conditionals

The two halves can point at different times:

- A past condition with a present result: *Si **hubiera estudiado** medicina, ahora **sería** médica.*
- A permanent condition with a past result: *Si **fuera** más alto, me **habrían elegido** para el equipo.*

Ask of each half whether it is about then, or about always or now.

## Regret, reproach and 'as if'

- **ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive** means if only (about the past): *Ojalá **hubiera ido**.*
- **como si + pluperfect subjunctive**: *Me miró **como si hubiera visto** un fantasma.*
- **de + haber + participle** (written style, replaces si): ***De haberlo sabido**, no habría venido.*
- For a reproach, use **deberías haber** or **tendrías que haber** + participle: *Deberías haberme avisado.* Pronouns attach to haber.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiese llegado a tiempo, habría firmado el contrato.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If he had arrived in time, he would have signed the contract.

vocabulary.meaning: would have (perfect conditional of haber, + participle)
vocabulary.example: Con un poco más de suerte, habríamos ganado la final.
vocabulary.example_meaning: With a bit more luck, we would have won the final.

vocabulary.meaning: if only (+ pluperfect subjunctive for the past)
vocabulary.example: Ojalá hubiéramos sacado las entradas antes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If only we had bought the tickets earlier.

vocabulary.example: Se comportó como si no hubiera pasado nada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She behaved as if nothing had happened.

vocabulary.meaning: had I known, if I had known
vocabulary.example: De haberlo sabido, habría traído el paraguas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Had I known, I'd have brought the umbrella.

vocabulary.example: Debería haber revisado el informe antes de enviarlo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I should have checked the report before sending it.

vocabulary.meaning: you should have, you ought to have (+ participle)
vocabulary.example_meaning: You ought to have asked for help.

vocabulary.example: Me arrepiento de no haber estudiado alemán.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I regret not having studied German.

vocabulary.meaning: to throw something back at someone, to reproach
vocabulary.example: Siempre me echa en cara que no fui a su boda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He always throws it in my face that I didn't go to his wedding.

vocabulary.example: Si hubiera empezado en enero, a estas alturas ya habría terminado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If I'd started in January, I'd have finished by now.

vocabulary.example: Si el médico hubiera llegado a tiempo, todo habría sido distinto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If the doctor had arrived in time, everything would have been different.

vocabulary.example: Perdió la oportunidad de su vida por no contestar el correo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He missed the chance of a lifetime by not answering the email.

quiz.prompt: Si ___ (saber, yo) que venías, habría hecho una tarta.
quiz.explanation: A condition about a past that did not happen takes si + pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera (or hubiese) sabido.
hints: Use haber in the past subjunctive + participle.

quiz.prompt: Si me hubieras avisado, te ___ a buscar al aeropuerto.
quiz.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition takes the perfect conditional: habría ido (hubiera ido is also heard).

quiz.prompt: Which counterfactual about the past is correct?
options: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
Si lo habría sabido, no hubiera venido.
Si lo había sabido, no habría venido.
quiz.correct_answer: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
quiz.explanation: The si-clause takes the pluperfect subjunctive; habría never goes after si.
hints: Which form can never follow si?

quiz.prompt: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora ___ (ser, yo) médica.
quiz.explanation: This is a mixed conditional. A past condition with a present result (ahora) takes the simple conditional, sería.

quiz.prompt: Si ___ más alto, me habrían elegido para el equipo. (I am short; I always have been.)
quiz.explanation: A permanent condition uses the imperfect subjunctive (fuera) even when the result is in the past. Sería and habría sido never follow si.
hints: It is a lasting trait, and it follows si.

quiz.explanation: A wish about the past takes ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive: hubiéramos ido.
hints: Anoche means last night, so the chance is gone.
The nosotros form carries an accent: -éramos.

quiz.prompt: Me miró como si ___ un fantasma.
quiz.explanation: Como si always takes the past subjunctive. For an earlier event it takes the pluperfect: hubiera visto.
hints: Como si never takes the indicative.

quiz.prompt: ___ sabido, no habría venido. (written style, without si: 'had I known it')
quiz.explanation: De + haber + participle replaces a si-clause, and the pronoun attaches to haber: de haberlo sabido.
hints: Use de + an infinitive with lo attached.

quiz.explanation: Debería(s) haber + participle is a reproach about the past: 'should have'.
hints: It is a complaint, not a guess.

listening.text: Si hubiera llovido, no habríamos salido.
listening.meaning: If it had rained, we wouldn't have gone out.

listening.text: Ojalá me lo hubieras contado antes.
listening.meaning: I wish you had told me earlier.

listening.text: Habla como si lo hubiera visto todo.
listening.meaning: He talks as if he had seen it all.

listening.text: Si hubieras salido antes, no habrías perdido el tren.
listening.meaning: If you had left earlier, you wouldn't have missed the train.

listening.text: De haberlo imaginado, habría reservado mesa.
listening.meaning: Had I imagined it, I'd have booked a table.

listening.text: Si no fuera tan cabezota, ya lo habría arreglado.
listening.meaning: If he weren't so stubborn, he would have fixed it by now.

listening.text: Tendrías que haber llamado al fontanero hace una semana.
listening.meaning: You should have called the plumber a week ago.
listening.note: New word: el fontanero = the plumber.

listening.text: Si hubiera aceptado aquel trabajo, ahora viviría en Buenos Aires.
listening.meaning: If I had accepted that job, I'd be living in Buenos Aires now.
listening.note: A mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

guide.tip: After si, use hubiera, never habría.

conversations.title: The missed flight
conversations.scenario: Elena and Javier have just missed their flight to Tenerife and are sitting in the airport café.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Si hubiéramos salido de casa a las seis, ahora estaríamos en el avión.
lines.meaning: If we had left home at six, we'd be on the plane now.
lines.note: A mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ya, pero si no hubieras vuelto a por el cargador, habríamos llegado.
lines.meaning: Yes, but if you hadn't gone back for the charger, we'd have made it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Me lo vas a echar en cara toda la tarde?
lines.meaning: Are you going to throw it in my face all afternoon?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, perdona. Es que tendríamos que haber facturado por internet.
lines.meaning: No, sorry. It's just that we should have checked in online.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: De haberlo sabido, habría pedido un taxi en vez de ir en metro.
lines.meaning: Had I known, I'd have ordered a taxi instead of taking the underground.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá hubiera comprado el billete flexible. Costaba solo veinte euros más.
lines.meaning: If only I had bought the flexible ticket. It was only twenty euros more.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bueno, el de la ventanilla nos habló como si hubiéramos perdido el último vuelo del año.
lines.meaning: Well, the man at the desk talked to us as if we'd missed the last flight of the year.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y hay otro a las nueve. Si fuera más dramático, habría llorado.
lines.meaning: And there's another one at nine. If I were more dramatic, I'd have cried.
lines.note: A mixed conditional: permanent condition, past result.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues a estas alturas, mejor pedimos algo de cenar.
lines.meaning: Well, at this stage, we'd better order something for dinner.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Buena idea. Y la próxima vez, salimos a las cinco.
lines.meaning: Good idea. And next time, we leave at five.

bites.title: Hubiera + participle
bites.rule: An unreal past condition takes si + hubiera (or hubiese) + participle, then habría + participle.
bites.example_meaning: If I had known, I would have come.

bites.title: Never si + habría
bites.rule: Habría can go in the main clause (and so can hubiera), but never right after si.
bites.example: Si hubieras llamado, te habría abierto.
bites.example_meaning: If you had called, I'd have opened the door.

bites.title: Mixed times
bites.rule: A past condition can have a present result (si hubiera estudiado, ahora sería…), and a lasting condition a past result (si fuera alto, habría jugado…).
bites.example: Si hubiera ahorrado, ahora tendría un coche.
bites.example_meaning: If I had saved, I'd have a car now.

bites.title: Ojalá, como si, debería haber
bites.rule: Ojalá and como si take the pluperfect subjunctive for the past. Debería haber or tendrías que haber + participle means should have.
bites.example_meaning: I wish I had gone with you.

sorts.title: Which half of the sentence?
sorts.why: Hubiera or hubiese goes after si. Habría and the simple conditional go in the result.

sorts.title: When is the result?

items.text: Si hubiera ahorrado, me habría comprado el piso.
Si hubiera ahorrado, ahora tendría dinero.
Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos ido a la playa.
Si no hubiera dejado el inglés, ahora lo hablaría bien.
Si hubieras venido, te habrías divertido.

sorts.why: Habría + participle is a past result, and the simple conditional (tendría, hablaría) is a present one.

spots.sentence: Si lo habría sabido, no hubiera venido.
spots.why: Habría never follows si. The si-clause takes the pluperfect subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Ojalá habías venido a la fiesta.
spots.why: Ojalá takes the subjunctive: hubieras venido.

spots.sentence: Me miró como si había visto un fantasma.
spots.why: Como si takes the past subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Si hubiera estudiado más, ahora tendré un buen trabajo.
spots.why: A present result of an unreal condition takes the conditional.

spots.sentence: Si hubieras salido antes, no habrás perdido el tren.
spots.why: The result takes the perfect conditional, not the future perfect.

builds.meaning: If I had known, I would have come.
I wish you had called me earlier.

builds.text: Me miró como si hubiera visto un fantasma.
builds.meaning: He looked at me as if he had seen a ghost.
You should have warned me earlier.
